notes:
SOURCE STRUCTURE. The article is a 温活 (warming-practice) listicle. Its warming attributions come mainly from list membership under the explicit heading 「【最強の温活食材】効率的に体を温めるおすすめの食べ物一覧」 (L66), which has four sub-sections: 根菜類 (L71) / 発酵食品 (L82) / たんぱく質 (L92) / スパイス・薬味 (L103). Items in those bullet lists are coded warm on the heading, per the two-column/column-header logic of §3. Cooling attributions are all in running prose (L156 fruit, L162 drinks, L171 白砂糖, L178 生野菜).

THE 陽/陰 TABLE (L137-151) YIELDS NO CODABLE FOOD. The table 「体を温めやすい食材（陽）｜体を冷やしやすい食材（陰）」 has row headers 色 / 産地 / 形状 / 水分量 — these are ATTRIBUTE row headers, not foods, and they appear identically on both the warm and the cool side, so per the rules they are structural row headers and are not coded. The cells contain descriptors (赤、オレンジ、黒、黄 / 青、白、緑 / 寒い地域 / 暑い地域 / 丸いもの / 長いもの / 水分が少なく… / 水分が多く…), not food names. The only food-ish token in the table is 「（根菜）」 inside the warm 形状 cell (L147); it duplicates 根菜類 already coded from L72, so no separate row was created.

HEDGED / NEGATED-COOL ATTRIBUTIONS — FLAGGED FOR ADJUDICATION. Four rows are coded warm on a NEGATED cooling statement rather than a positive warming statement: リンゴ / ブドウ / プルーン (L154-155, 「体を冷やしにくく温活中にもおすすめです」) and ドライフルーツ (L156, 「生の果物に比べて体を冷やしにくい特徴があります」). The source never says these warm the body; it says they cool it LESS. They differ from the §8 substitute-recommendation case in that a temperature-nature claim IS made, so they were coded, but an adjudicator may prefer neutral or exclusion. ドライフルーツ's claim is explicitly comparative against 「生の果物」; 生の果物 is NOT coded because the source only makes it the comparison baseline and never states its direction.

EXCLUDED PER §8 (substitute recommendation, no nature attribution). L172-173: てんさい糖, はちみつ, 全粒粉, 玄米, そば are recommended only as replacements for 白砂糖 / 精製小麦粉 on a vitamin-mineral rationale, with no warming/cooling nature stated. 玄米 recurs at L233 (「玄米のビタミンB群がエネルギー代謝をサポート」) — again metabolic, not thermal. Not coded. (Note 白砂糖 itself IS coded cool, because L171 states 「冷えを感じやすくなる」.) Also excluded: 精製された白い食品 / 精製小麦粉 (L170-173, no direction stated).

EXCLUDED PER §8 (prepared beverages / dishes, not a food's nature). 生姜湯 (L159, L236), 白湯 (L236), ホットココア (L236 — prepared AND hot), 味噌汁 (L90, L241), 豚汁 and おでん (L231, recommended as コンビニ温活メニュー but no nature attribution — they are hot prepared dishes), スパイスの効いた料理 (L241). Plain ココア (L159) IS coded warm because it sits verbatim in the 「温活向きの飲み物」 enumeration alongside the teas, parallel to how coffee/tea are treated as foods elsewhere in the frame; if the adjudicator treats cocoa as a prepared beverage it should be dropped.

OTHER NON-ATTRIBUTIONS DELIBERATELY NOT CODED. たんぱく質 IS coded warm (L92 heading 「熱を生み出す源となるたんぱく質」 + L251 「体を内側から温める働きがあります」) even though it is a macronutrient rather than a food — flagged in case the study excludes nutrient labels; 糖質 (L60) and 脂質 (L62) appear only in the DIT percentage table with no thermal-nature claim and are NOT coded. ゆで卵 and 冷奴 (L99) are listed only for convenience (「調理の手間が少なく」), not direction — not coded (冷奴 is a chilled dish appearing inside the warming protein section, which would be contradictory to code). オリーブオイル / アマニ油 (L128) are recommended for fat-soluble-vitamin absorption, no direction — not coded. 刺身 vs 焼き魚 / 煮魚 (L247) is a cooking-method recommendation, not a nature attribution — not coded. おにぎり / お弁当 (L232) are microwave-reheating advice = serving temperature. BASE FOOD product names (ベースブレッド, BASE YAKISOBA, BASE RAMEN, BASE Cookies, BASE Pound Cake, BASE Pancake Mix) are advertising with nutrient claims only, no warm/cool nature — not coded.

CONDITION SPLITS. 生姜 (L105-106) says raw ginger's gingerol changes on heating so the body warms from deeper within, i.e. the source implies heated ginger is stronger — but it never assigns raw ginger a COOLING direction, so only one warm row is recorded (no raw/cooked split). バナナ (L157) has 「焼きバナナのように加熱して取り入れる方法もおすすめです」 — a preparation workaround, not a second direction; バナナ stays a single cool row.

NO NEUTRAL ROWS. The source never uses 平 / 中庸 / どちらでもない.
